dedupe_keys.name: openipsl open instance power system library

description: OpenIPSL, the Open-Instance Power System Library, is a library of power system component models written in the Modelica language for dynamic analysis such as phasor time-domain simulation. It is developed for research and education with the goal of maximising compatibility with Modelica tools, and it provides reference power system models for the development and testing of Modelica compilers. It is developed and maintained by Luigi Vanfretti's research group ALSETLab at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in Troy, New York, with collaborators such as Dietmar Winkler. The library is location-independent: any power system can be assembled from its components. Code is on GitHub (citation file version 2.0.0, commits to April 2026) under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost, with a citation paper by de Castro, Winkler, Laera, Vanfretti and others. Caveats: the library contains only models, with no power flow or time-domain solvers, so a Modelica tool is required; it is fully compatible with Dymola, its primary development environment, and largely compatible with OpenModelica. Simulation uses are dynamic network simulation and stability studies for resilience analysis. Related records: it compares with model-transient-library and complements model-andes, a Python tool for similar phasor dynamics.
